name: Voce Viva
remarks: L'Oréal launch, September 2020, face Lady Gaga. Press release describes it as floral woody. 'Moss' stands for the brand's 'crystal moss accord'. Retailers list base as crystal moss, vanilla, tonka; the press release adds sandalwood. Still sold, flankers include Voce Viva Intensa (2021).

name: Miss Dior Chérie
remarks: Original 2005 formula (caramelised popcorn and wild strawberry sorbet accord). Reformulated by François Demachy in 2011 and renamed simply 'Miss Dior' (Wikipedia says 2011, often cited as 2012); the original 1947 Miss Dior became 'Miss Dior Originale'. The 2005 Nagel version is no longer produced.

name: Féerie
remarks: Launched August 2008 (Givaudan). Launch press lists red berries instead of blackcurrant/orange. Current availability of the original EDP not confirmed; later flankers include Féerie Rose des Neiges and Féerie Rubis (2015).

name: Manifesto L'Élixir
remarks: Sold as 'Eau de Parfum Intense' (fall 2013). Perfumer not credited in the sources consulted. Reseller listings mark it as discontinued ('eingestellt'), not confirmed on YSL's site; it no longer appears in current YSL ranges as far as the sources show.

name: Canoë
remarks: Created in Paris in 1935 by Jean Carles (Roure); US launch 1936, which is the year often quoted. The two sources place lavender differently (top vs heart) and the current Dana pyramid is shorter (bergamot, petitgrain / lavender, geranium / patchouli, musk); the merged pyramid follows the original description. Still sold by Dana Classic Fragrances, reorchestrated (2000 re-orchestration noted by Perfume Intelligence).

name: Aura
perfumer: Daphné Bugey, Amandine Clerc-Marie, Christophe Raynaud, Marie Salamagne
remarks: Launched June 2017 (UK/France), 'botanical meets animal' concept; Tiger Liana and Wolfwood are Firmenich captives. Pyramid as listed by Escentual/Lookfantastic (Faces puts rhubarb on top). Family label from Osmoz editorial ('woody and aromatic'), no brand family found. Retailer (Faces) lists the EDP as discontinued; a later Aura Eau de Toilette is a different juice.

name: Bois d'Argent
remarks: Created 2004 for the Dior Homme collection (Hedi Slimane), originally an eau de cologne marketed to men; now an Eau de Parfum in La Collection Privée, sold as unisex. Dior credits the founding trio to Hedi Slimane with Francis Kurkdjian and Annick Ménardo; Ménardo is the usual credit for Bois d'Argent. Reformulated (EDP 2010, then Demachy 2018 and Kurkdjian 2022 according to one source). Still sold.

name: The Beat
perfumer: Dominique Ropion, Olivier Polge, Béatrice Piquet
remarks: Women's version (a men's The Beat followed in 2008). Built around a Ceylon tea accord and an iris accord (IFF). Family label assigned from the published notes, no brand family found. Still listed by US discount retailers; production status not confirmed by Burberry.

name: Fleur du Mâle
remarks: Flanker of Le Mâle, unveiled February 2007 by BPI. Official pyramid is minimal (orange blossom over petitgrain and coumarin in a fern accord). Discontinued for several years; Jean Paul Gaultier announced its return in 2026 (Paris Select Book), formula of the relaunch not confirmed.

name: Dune
perfumer: Jean-Louis Sieuzac, Dominique Ropion, Nejla Barbir
remarks: Launched spring 1991. Dior/Sephora classify it as floral amber. Some sources add wallflower, lichen/oakmoss and amber. Still sold as Eau de Toilette (reformulated over the years).

name: L'Extase
remarks: Unveiled January 2015, on sale March 2015 at Galeries Lafayette (Osmoz gives 2014 as creation year). Kurkdjian's first Nina Ricci; face Laetitia Casta. Brand describes a 'Barely Rose' accord (white petals, Turkish and Bulgarian rose, pink pepper) and a 'Musky Shadow' accord (benzoin, cedar, musk, amber). Flanker Caresse de Roses (2016). Likely no longer produced, not confirmed.

name: Acqua di Gioia
perfumer: Loc Dong, Anne Flipo, Dominique Ropion
remarks: Launched June 2010 (IFF). 'Sugar' is a brown sugar accord. Osmoz lists the EDP as the main version; flankers Eau Fraîche (2013), Eau de Toilette (2014), Essenza. Still sold.

name: Trésor in Love
remarks: Flanker of Trésor (1990), IFF, face Elettra Wiedemann. Osmoz's 'rose-bay' is a translation of 'baies roses' (pink pepper), confirmed by Notino. Production status not confirmed.

name: Love, Chloé
remarks: Launched September 2010 (Givaudan). 'Powdery Notes' stands for the talc accord; heliotrope listed as heliotropine. Flankers Eau Intense (2011) and L'Eau Florale (2013). Production status not confirmed.

name: Insolence
remarks: Original EDT (2006), face Hilary Swank, bottle by Serge Mansau. Wikipedia (Guerlain article reached via the Samsara URL) credits Maurice Roucel; Sylvaine Delacourte co-credited by Osmoz. An EDP (2008) is a different composition. Still sold.

name: Van Cleef
remarks: Women's 'Van Cleef' (1993), Osmoz family 'Floral - Orange Tuberose'; Perfume Intelligence calls it fruity floral with an oriental character. Note lists differ: Perfume Intelligence gives raspberry, tagetes, rose, lily of the valley, hyacinth, vetiver, sandalwood, amber. Perfume Intelligence credits André Girodroux, not corroborated, so perfumer left null. Existed as EDP and EDT. Not in the current Van Cleef & Arpels range as far as seen; discontinuation not formally confirmed.

name: Ambre Nuit
remarks: La Collection Privée (now La Collection Privée Christian Dior). Dior's official notes: Calabrian bergamot, Turkish Damask rose essence, ambergris, guaiac wood, cedar, patchouli; Dior classifies it 'amber woody floral'. Osmoz lists an early Eau de Cologne range and files it under men, but it is sold as unisex EDP. Still sold.

name: Manifesto
remarks: IFF, Europe launch September 2012, US early 2013. Reported as discontinued by review/reseller sites, not confirmed by YSL.

name: J'adore L'Absolu
remarks: Only one clean source reached (Osmoz FR, via search summary; page itself blocked). Reworking of J'adore (1999) around four absolutes: ylang-ylang, Turkish rose, jasmine sambac, tuberose. An Osmoz magazine page mentions 2018, likely confusing it with a later J'adore release; 2007 is the creation year on the product page. Production status not confirmed; needs a second source for year and notes.

name: Miss Dior Absolutely Blooming
remarks: Flanker of Miss Dior (2012 Miss Dior line). 'Centifolia Rose' = May rose (Grasse rose absolute / Damask rose per some listings). Do not confuse with Miss Dior Blooming Bouquet (2014, EDT). Sources are retailer listings only; one review site says it was later discontinued, not confirmed by Dior.

name: Bella
remarks: Third 'princess' of Les Belles de Nina (July 2018, travel retail first). Heart is a rose jelly accord (Turkish rose oil and rose absolute). Flanker Bella Sorbet exists. Production status not confirmed.

name: Boss Alive
remarks: Launched February 2020. Osmoz places Bourbon vanilla in the top; Escentual and most retailers put vanilla in the base, followed here. Olive Tree = olive wood. Still sold.

name: Pure XS for Her
remarks: Feminine counterpart of Pure XS (2017), September 2018, Givaudan; face Emily Ratajkowski. Brand now 'Rabanne'. Retailers order the pyramid differently (some place vanilla in the base). Still sold.

name: Dahlia Noir
remarks: Only one clean source reached (Osmoz); second source not found before the search budget ran out. Flankers Dahlia Noir EDT (2012), L'Eau (2013); Dahlia Divin (2014) is a separate line. Production status not confirmed.

name: Cinéma
remarks: Only one clean source reached (Osmoz). 'Almond' = almond blossom. Perfumer commonly credited to Jacques Cavallier but not verified in a clean source, so left null. Campaign with Michelle Alves by Jean-Baptiste Mondino. Flankers EDT (2006) and Scénario d'Été. Production status not confirmed.

name: Oud Ispahan
remarks: La Collection Privée. Both sources come from Osmoz (product page + magazine), so not fully independent. Still sold by Dior.

name: Midnight in Paris
remarks: Only one clean source reached (Osmoz, IFF). Named after a Van Cleef & Arpels watch. Sold as EDT and, in some countries, EDP. Production status not confirmed.

name: Samsara
remarks: Built around Mysore sandalwood and jasmine; Wikipedia credits Jean-Paul Guerlain (with Anne-Marie Saget) and confirms jasmine, ylang-ylang, sandalwood. Still sold, reformulated (sandalwood sourcing changed).

name: Eau de Cartier
remarks: Only one clean source reached (Osmoz, Quest International). Many flankers (Essence d'Orange 2010, Essence de Bois 2012, Goutte de Rose 2013, an Eau de Parfum by Mathilde Laurent). Production status of the original EDT not confirmed.

name: Boss Bottled Infinite
remarks: Flanker of Boss Bottled (1998), April 2019, Coty; face Chris Hemsworth. Bloomingdale's classifies it aromatic woody. Olive Tree = olivewood. Still sold.
